channel.title: Kelroy James: Writing
channel.description: Essays on supply chain assurance, third-party risk and governance.

item.title: The Physical Assurance Gap in Third-Party Risk
item.description: Two 2026 KPMG surveys map where third-party risk management spends its attention: data, AI, managed services, almost none on physical supplier verification.

item.title: The Convergence of Cyber-GRC and Physical Logistics
item.description: Why siloed supply chain assurance creates blind spots, where they form, and what happens to custody when nobody is holding the item.

item.title: Supplier Concentration Risk: Measuring It Tier by Tier
item.description: A supplier list with fifty names can still fail from a single point. How to measure the concentration that headcount hides, and what to do about it.

item.title: The Enterprise Risk Management We Already Do
item.description: Corporate risk management is being rewired around decisions, dependencies and judgement. Operational institutions have worked that way for decades.

item.title: Engineering Trust: What Military Assurance and AI Governance Share
item.description: Deloitte and BCG argue AI is turning assurance into a property of the system itself. Naval logistics assurance meets the same limit from the other end.

item.title: A Ship's Mind, Before Anyone Could Govern One
item.description: Two Royal Navy admirals, two years apart, both reached for AI at the heart of a warship. The record corrects which one said it first.

item.title: Recognition Before Retraining
item.description: Why the Pan-Defence Skills Framework is the missing piece in service leaver transition, for anyone leaving with a trade nobody outside recognises.

item.title: Talent Should Flow Both Ways
item.description: The Pan-Defence Skills Framework as a Defence Industrial Strategy tool, connecting service leavers to the industrial base that needs their exact skills.

item.title: Dangerous Goods Training and a Foundation Degree, at the Same Time
item.description: In 2018, as sole logistics contact for Fleet Diving Squadron HQ, I delivered dangerous goods training to EOD personnel while finishing a Foundation Degree.

item.title: Five People, Every Deployed Platform
item.description: In 2019, five members of the Fleet Stores Coordination Cell at Northwood received the Herbert Lott Efficiency Award for supporting every deployed platform.

item.title: Study Shapes Practice, Practice Shapes Delivery
item.description: A career of study alongside service, what it produced, and why development is a retention lever the Navy has not yet used.

item.title: Building the Tracking System Fleet Diving Squadron Didn't Have
item.description: In 2017, as Logistics Specialist at Fleet Diving Squadron, I built a consignment-tracking system the unit didn't have, tested live on exercise in Latvia.

item.title: A Dissertation About the Job I Was Already Doing
item.description: While working in Fleet Operations at Northwood, I completed a BSc in Logistics and Operations Management, built around the job I was already doing.

item.title: The Course They Almost Didn't Let Me On
item.description: The Defence Logistics Staff Course is built for high calibre officers of SO2/3 rank. A Petty Officer's case for a place, and what five modules taught.

item.title: Supply Chain Management Was Already a Discipline
item.description: What five MIT courses in supply chain analytics and design named in work I had already been doing for years, and why logisticians shouldn't wait to start.

item.title: Trade Finance and Assurance: Why Faster Rails Have Not Closed the Gap
item.description: Digital trade documents and tokenised payments have modernised the rails, yet the trade finance gap has not moved. A practitioner view of de-risking, correspondent banking and assurance.
